title: Card Flipping Game
statement:
There are `n` cards on a table. Card `i` shows the positive integer `fronts[i]` on its upper side and has `backs[i]` on its hidden side. You may turn over any set of cards, including none of them.

Once you have finished turning cards, call an integer **good** when it is on the hidden side of at least one card and on the upper side of no card. Over every way of turning cards, find the smallest integer that can be good, and return it. Return `0` if no choice of turns makes any integer good.
notes:
## Intuition

Trying all 2^n ways to turn the cards is hopeless for 1000 cards, so ask instead which values can ever be good. A card with the same number on both sides always shows that number, so that number can **never** be good. Any other value `x` that appears on some card can always be made good: turn every card that carries `x` so that `x` is hidden. A card has `x` on only one side (otherwise it would be a same-both-sides card), so this never forces `x` face up, and the other cards cannot show `x` at all. The answer is therefore the smallest card value that is not on a same-both-sides card.

## Approach

1. Put every value of a card with `fronts[i] === backs[i]` into the set `blocked`.
2. Scan all card values on both sides and keep the smallest one not in `blocked` as `best`.
3. Return `best`, or `0` if no value qualified.

## Example 1, step by step

`fronts = [1,2,4,4,7]`, `backs = [1,3,4,1,3]`.

- Cards 0 and 2 have equal sides, so `blocked = {1, 4}`.
- Scanning values: 1 is blocked, 2 is allowed (`best = 2`), 3, 4, 7 and the rest are larger or blocked.

The answer is `2`: turn card 1 so its 2 is hidden, and no card shows 2.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): two passes over the cards with constant-time set lookups.
- Space: O(n) for `blocked`.

## Pitfalls

- A value is ruled out only by a card with that value on **both** sides; showing it on one side of some card is fine, because that card can be turned.
- Check values from both arrays: the answer may come from `fronts` as easily as from `backs`.
- Return `0`, not `Infinity`, when every value is blocked.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `blocked` | values printed on both sides of some card; they can never be good |
| `best` | smallest allowed value seen so far |
| `i` | index of the card being examined |
